title: How much math you actually need, precisely

claims.text: The method underlying model training was introduced by Cauchy on 18 October 1847 in a note on the general method for resolving systems of simultaneous equations, and was later named the method of descent by Hadamard.

source.title: Cauchy, A. L., Méthode générale pour la résolution des systèmes d’équations simultanées, Comptes Rendus de l’Académie des Sciences, Paris, 25:536-538, 1847

claims.text: The attribution is not simple: historians of numerical analysis trace steepest descent to Cauchy in 1829 as a means of solving a nonlinear equation, and note that the form in use today was introduced by Kantorovich in 1945, with Curry’s 1944 paper on steepest descent for non-linear minimization problems an earlier milestone in the nonlinear case.

source.title: Cauchy, A. L., Méthode générale pour la résolution des systèmes d’équations simultanées, Comptes Rendus de l’Académie des Sciences, Paris, 25:536-538, 1847

claims.text: Matrix multiplication, matrix addition, the unit matrix, the inverse and powers of matrices were introduced by Cayley in a memoir of 1858, which also explored the non-commutative algebra associated with matrix multiplication.

source.title: Cayley, A., A Memoir on the Theory of Matrices, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London 148:17-37, 1858

beats.broke: the question is asked as how much math, which has no answer, because the amount depends entirely on which of three quite different jobs you intend to do
beats.fix: name the job first — using a model, diagnosing one, or deriving a method — because each needs a different and specifiable set
beats.cost: the honest answer is smaller than the intimidating version and larger than the dismissive one, and it satisfies nobody
beats.interview: what actually goes wrong for people who skipped the math
